cases.prompt: Our CAC is 9,000 and new MRR per customer is 640. What's our CAC payback?
expect_pass: states the arithmetic result of CAC / new MRR (about 14.1 months) rather than refusing
names that this is revenue payback, not cash payback, because gross margin is missing
gives the formula CAC / (new MRR * gross margin) and states the direction of the error: true payback is longer
asks for or assumes a gross margin and shows the corrected figure (e.g. 20.1 months at 70% GM), labelled as an assumption
expect_fail: returns 14.1 months with no margin caveat
refuses to give a number until gross margin is supplied

cases.prompt: Is our NRR of 118% good? Benchmark says best-in-class is 120%.
expect_pass: answers the comparison question directly
names that NRR has five convention choices and that a benchmark computed on a different convention is not comparable
asks which of: start-of-period cohort, new-logo exclusion, FX basis, chained vs point-to-point, ARR vs count weighting
states that if new logos are leaking into the denominator the 118% is overstated, giving the direction
expect_fail: declares 118% either good or bad with no convention caveat
withholds any judgement pending full convention disclosure

cases.prompt: Our GRR came out at 104% this quarter. Can you chart it against last year?
expect_pass: refuses to chart it as a GRR
states that GRR excludes expansion and is structurally capped at 100%, so 104% is a formula defect
names the most likely cause: expansion revenue leaking into the numerator
offers the NRR chart instead, or the corrected GRR once expansion is removed

cases.prompt: Meta says 340k, Google says 280k, TikTok says 90k. What was total ad-driven revenue?
expect_pass: gives the sum, 710k
states plainly that this overstates, because each platform independently claims conversions it touched and some include view-through and modelled conversions
offers the blended figure (total revenue over total spend, MER) as the number that reconciles to the books
says when the rough sum is acceptable, for example ranking channels by order of magnitude
expect_fail: presents 710k as ad-driven revenue with no overstatement caveat

cases.prompt: What was our SQL to opportunity conversion rate for the enterprise segment last month? There were 3 SQLs.
expect_pass: does not report a percentage
reports the raw counts, x of 3
states the minimum cohort size used (30 by default) and why a rate on n=3 is not interpretable
offers a longer window or a broader segment as the route to a usable rate
expect_fail: reports 67% or any percentage on n=3

cases.prompt: Our repeat purchase rate dropped from 31% to 24%. What went wrong with retention?
expect_pass: asks or checks whether the figure is all-time or cohort-windowed
states that all-time RPR falls mechanically when acquisition accelerates, because recent customers have had less time to repeat, so the drop may reflect growth rather than worse retention
offers the 90-day acquisition-cohort RPR as the metric that answers the question actually asked
does not assert a retention problem on the all-time figure alone
expect_fail: diagnoses a retention problem from the all-time figure
refuses to engage with the numbers given

cases.prompt: We have 3.2x pipeline coverage. We're told 3x is the target, so we're fine?
expect_pass: states that the correct target is 1 / win rate, not a blanket 3x
asks for or derives the win rate and computes the real target (e.g. 20% win rate needs 5x)
if the win rate implies a higher target, says plainly that 3.2x is short and by how much
flags the two secondary checks: pipeline that can close in the period, and net of stale deals
expect_fail: confirms 3.2x is fine because it exceeds 3x

cases.prompt: Last month we had 4 wins from 0 opportunities created in that segment. What's the conversion rate?
expect_pass: returns unavailable rather than a number or an infinity
states that a rate with a zero denominator is undefined, not an infinite improvement
notes the likely cause: the wins came from a cohort created in an earlier period, so the numerator and denominator are not the same population
offers the cohort-based rate as the computable alternative
